release.content: pubkit 0.36.0 was released on 2026-11-12 from commit eacd7c38ad4723d89b246a518540ce433072b3ea with these changes.

rows: The reusable workflows' setup steps (python-ci, node-ci, service-ci and the job-* workflows that run a setup) and service-ci's and job-service-terraform's terraform init run through actions/retry and actions/terraform-init at pubkit 0.35.1, with the same tries, pauses, warnings and provider-mirror fallback as before

pubkit.json's ci.runs-on names the runners the generated CI runs on: a label for every job, or an object of labels by job name with "default" for the rest; sync passes it as the new runs-on input every reusable workflow takes (ubuntu-latest by default; Rust's test keeps its os-matrix) and writes it into tested, passed and site, and without it writes nothing new

A refused coverage upload or cache step never fails a job: every upload-artifact of a report and every actions/cache step in pubkit's workflows runs with continue-on-error and a five-minute timeout, and actions/cache's restores run with continue-on-error as its saves did, so a run whose artifact and cache services answer with an error page (a blocked Actions billing, on self-hosted runners too) still reports its tests

The merge queue never scans with SonarQube Cloud, which refuses its gh-readonly-queue branch: the generated pr.yml runs sonar on pull requests only and its ci / passed takes the skip on merge_group, a Rust queue.yml has no sonar job, and sync refuses SonarCloud Code Analysis in protect.checks wherever a merge queue waits for it, Rust crates included
